newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Roadblock protest springs up again in Argentina.
newsitem.headline: Roadblock protest springs up again in Argentina.

text.p: Hundreds of Argentines in Cordoba province blocked a highway with burning tires on Wednesday in the latest outbreak of protests against the country's high unemployment rate.

About 800 impoverished protesters in the town of Cruz del Eje decided late on Tuesday to put back a roadblock they had lifted 17 days ago when they began negotiations with the provincial government on ways to bring jobs to the area.
Provincial Gov. Ramon Mestre told Clarin newspaper talks had reached deadlock. "There isn't anything else to offer."

He said the protesters shared the blame for unemployment and had turned up their noses at labouring for local cotton and olive farmers. "Who is going to invest in a place where the people don't want to work?" Mestre asked.

The wave of unrest and protests over unemployment in the Argentine provinces began two months ago when demonstrators clased with police in the southern province of Neuquen. Roadblocks then spread to Jujuy, Salta and Cordoba provinces.
The national government was forced to promise aid to Jujuy to help create 10,000 jobs and end a long and violent series of roadblocks in the poor nothern province in late May.

President Carlos Menem's Cabinet was due to hold its next weekly meeting in Cordoba province on Thursday with Menem adamant he would not be pressured by the roadblockers. "We are not going continue to allow the national government and the provincial governments to be blackmailed in this way," he was quoted as saying in the Clarin newspaper.

Argentina's unemployment rate has soared under Menem's Peronist Party government to 17.3 percent and it is much worse in many of the poorer provinces. The government hopes that renewed economic growth and a plan to make labour contracts more flexible will eventually ease the jobless rate.
